description: Hashed API keys and a client-credentials grant let machine/service principals authenticate without a human session.

requirements.description: Service accounts must be able to authenticate without a human session using either hashed API keys or an OAuth2 client-credentials grant. API keys are generated as cryptographically random strings, displayed once, then stored only as an Argon2id hash. Client-credentials clients are registered per realm with a client ID and secret. Both credential types issue short-lived access tokens with explicitly assigned roles and scopes. API key and client operations are audited.
requirements.title: API Keys and Client-Credentials Grant for Machine Principals

validation.notes: api/internal/apikey/apikey_test.go: generate API key, verify the returned plaintext matches the stored hash; verify wrong key fails; verify correct key issues a token
api/internal/apikey/apikey_test.go: API key is shown in plaintext only at creation time; subsequent reads return only the key ID and metadata, never the secret
api/handlers/apikey/apikey_e2e_test.go: create API key via admin RPC, use it to call an authenticated endpoint → 200 with token; rotate (revoke + create new) → old key rejected, new key accepted

api/handlers/auth/client_credentials_e2e_test.go: register client, POST client-credentials grant with client ID + secret → access token issued with correct roles; use token on a protected endpoint → 200
bas/admin/api_key_management_test: admin creates an API key for a service account, copies the displayed secret, and uses it in a curl command to obtain a token; verifies revocation removes access

title: API Keys + Client-Credentials Grant
